source.check: returned unopposed: selected as the Unionist candidate for the division (Impartial Reporter, 8 May 1958, p. 7); the Reporter of 22 May 1958 (p. 7) states that 'all the members were returned unopposed for the County Council and the three Rural Councils'; sat as a member of the new council (Impartial Reporter, 10 July 1958, p. 3; Impartial Reporter, 12 February 1959, p. 5)

note: Triennial election of Lisnaskea Rural District Council, polled Thursday 5 June 1958. No contests. The Impartial Reporter of 22 May 1958, p. 7, records two changes — Mr. James Armstrong returned for Magheraveely in succession to Mr. John W. Irwin, and Mr. Thomas Maguire for Coolnamarrow in place of Mr. Denis Leonard — and notes that this was 'the first time for many years that Lisnaskea Council has been returned without an election'. Mr. Robert J. Liddle is returned unopposed for Derrylea (Reporter, 15 May 1958, p. 5). Other members are recorded where a selection list or a report of the new council's meetings names them, each division inferred from the 1955 return (Fermanagh Herald, 4 June 1955, p. 8). Filled from the Impartial Reporter's reports of Unionist selections (1, 8 and 15 May 1958): Ballindarragh, Corralongford, Maguiresbridge, Mullaghfad, Mullynagowan, Lisnaskea, Dresternan and Newtownbutler; each was returned unopposed (Impartial Reporter, 22 May 1958, p. 7). Dresternan and Newtownbutler were missing from the earlier record and are added. Recorded for Nationalist-held divisions from the selection lists and first-meeting reports in the Fermanagh Herald: Aghakillymaude, Clonkeelan, Derrysteaton, Kulmore, Roslea and Springtown. Recorded from reports of the new council's meetings during the term: Armagh Manor, Belleisle, Castle Balfour, Colebrooke, Crum, Dresternan, Drummully, Eshnadarragh, Greenhill and Newtownbutler. Mr. J. Whittendale (U) was co-opted at the first meeting (Impartial Reporter, 19 June 1958, p. 4); a co-option, not an election result. Returned unopposed.
